mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 8.5% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad economic slowdown, reducing corporate earnings growth and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both INDPRO and HOUST decline for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 2.0% and CPIAUCSL above 3.0% annually), the Federal Reserve's policy rate hikes compress equity valuations through higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% (annualized), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by a monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000, supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases by more than 100,000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 600,000 units signals weak residential construction, reducing economic activity and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST falls below 600.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with high inflation (CPIAUCSL above 3.0%) signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing the cost of capital and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (as indicated by high residential sales (RSAFS) and strong GDP growth (GDPC1)), the economy approaches capacity constraints, leading to inflationary pressures and potential Fed tightening, which causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS > 400,000 and GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% (annualized), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.
